Title: Model Base Design Unit Test Engineer
Description: Are you looking to work for a company that provides an innovative work environment, and your voice is heard? We have a position for a Engineer - Model-Based Design Unit Testing. This role is based in Guadalajara Mexico. Who we are: LER TechForce is an industry leader in embedded controls, software, functional safety, and engineering talent. For over 20 years LER has been working with customers across North America. Follow us at: LER TechForce on LinkedIn. What you will be doing: Engineer focused primarily on unit testing of model-based designs (Simulink), responsible for building and executing test strategies across MIL/SIL/PIL environments. This role is test-heavy, with secondary involvement in control model understanding and limited development support. The engineer ensures models are testable, verifiable, and compliant with quality standards such as ISO26262. Design and execute unit test cases for Simulink models. Review requirements for testability, completeness, and traceability. Develop and maintain MIL/SIL/PIL test frameworks and infrastructure. Build test harnesses using Simulink Test and MATLAB scripting. Validate control logic through structured simulation scenarios. Analyze test results, identify defects, and support root cause analysis. Collaborate with controls and system engineers to refine model/test interfaces. Support verification strategy development and continuous improvement. What you'll need to be successful: Essential: MATLAB/Simulink - strong proficiency required. Simulink-based unit testing methodologies. Test design derived from requirements. Real-time embedded control concepts, including loop rates, state-based control logic, and initialization/reset behavior. Understanding of model-based design workflows (MIL/SIL/PIL). Ability to analyze and debug control models. Preferred: Simulink Test Framework - test harness creation and management. MATLAB Unit Test Framework. MATLAB scripting for automation and regression testing. Simulink Coder - understanding generated code behavior. Experience with ISO26262 functional safety processes. Basic familiarity with embedded C/C++ for traceability to generated code. Exposure to closed-loop simulation and plant modeling concepts.
